topic.title: Logical Structure and Tractable Probabilistic Reasoning
topic.area: Graphical Models, Clustering, and Network Structure
topic.overview: Logical representations can expose repeated structure that makes otherwise expensive inference manageable. This topic includes lifted reasoning over groups of objects, compilation into tractable circuits, and learning models whose supported probability queries are efficient. The choice of representation determines not only speed but which questions can be answered with guarantees.
topic.whyItMatters: Exploiting symmetry can avoid expanding a compact relational description into an enormous ground model. Explicit tractability also helps distinguish a practical heuristic from a procedure that supports exact counting, conditional queries, or structured constraints.
topic.evolution: The collection includes early logic-learning and neural proof constructions, followed by 2010s work on lifting, decomposition trees, and sentential decision diagrams. Recent examples connect logical structure to diffusion guidance and classifier compression, while capability-certification results clarify limits of finite tests. These are related uses of logical structure, not an inferred citation lineage.
openQuestions: Which useful query families remain tractable after learning changes the model?
How can approximate symmetry be exploited without overstating exact inference guarantees?
